newsitem.title: PERU: Peru says captured 700 guerrillas this year.
newsitem.headline: Peru says captured 700 guerrillas this year.

text.p: The Peruvian government said Friday it had captured around 700 communist guerrillas so far in 1996 during a year of increased rebel activity.

"We will not let our guard down. We have solid hopes that we can soon say the awesome task of bringing peace to the country has been achieved," said Interior Minister Juan Briones Davila, according to government news agency Andina.
About 8,000 rebels from the Maoist Shining Path and the Cuban-style Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) groups have been jailed since Peru's guerrilla conflicts began in 1980, Briones added.

However, human rights groups claim the special "faceless" court system responsible for trying guerrilla suspects has jailed hundreds of innocent people on flimsy evidence, often obtained by torture, and without the chance of a fair trial.

Although greatly weakened since the 1992 capture of its leader Abimael Guzman, Shining Path has raised public fears of a comeback after a series of car-bombs, assassinations and clashes with security forces this year.
